taxonomy.note: GBIF match and species record 9685907: Falco sparverius Linnaeus, 1758, rank SPECIES, status ACCEPTED, order Falconiformes, family Falconidae. iNaturalist taxon 4665 (rank species, active) checked 2026-11-01.

external.note: gbif_usage_key 9685907 and inat_taxon_id 4665 checked at their providers. Wikidata Q651545 is the item for American kestrel.

conservation.note: Wikipedia: 'classed as least concern on the IUCN Red List'.

range.note: Only US, CA and MX are listed. Wikipedia names northern Canada, Alaska and the US as breeding range and describes Central and South American populations without a country list. Central and South American countries are omitted until a country-level source is checked.

traits.body_plan.note: A bird (class Aves, per GBIF) with two legs and wings. Wikipedia covers the species' hunting and flight behaviour, which fits this body plan.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; follows from the bird body plan and the schema's limb-count convention for birds.

traits.skin.note: Feathers: inherent to class Aves, not separately sourced.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endotherm: inherent to class Aves, not separately sourced.

traits.respiration.note: Lungs: inherent to class Aves, not separately sourced.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None: birds develop without metamorphosis, not separately sourced.

traits.flight.note: Powered: Wikipedia describes hovering with rapid wing beats and kiting, which require powered flight.

traits.perching.note: Wikipedia: 'The American kestrel's primary mode of hunting is by perching and waiting for prey to come near.'

traits.size_class.note: Small: computed from mass_kg 0.12 against the schema bound of 1 kg (Small < 1 kg, Tiny < 0.05 kg).

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: 'Most birds breeding in Canada and the northern United States migrate south in the winter ... Birds that breed south of about 35° north latitude are usually year-round residents.'

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia Reproduction: 'Incubation usually lasts 30 days ... After 28–31 days, their wings have developed and they are able to leave the nest.' No juvenile duration is given as a number here.

behavior.note: Authored program fsm-perch-hover-hunter-v1 (species/falco-sparverius/behavior.json). Hunting modes: Wikipedia 'perching and waiting' and 'kiting, hovering'; ADW 'hovering, perch-hunting, and in-flight insect catching'. Month sets and transitions are judgement; see the program description.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia: hunts by 'kiting, hovering in the air with rapid wing beats and scanning the ground for prey' and by perching. Walk is judgement for ground movement.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia: 'American kestrels are cavity nesters ... also commonly utilize nesting boxes.'

traits.mass_kg.note: Rounded midpoint of Wikipedia sex-specific ranges (male 80-143 g, female 86-165 g). Wikipedia gives no single typical mass.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Minimum 80 g (male) and maximum 165 g (female), from Wikipedia Description.

traits.lifespan_y.note: ADW (non-commercial, last resort): 'In the wild, their life expectancy is an average of 1 year and 3 months.' This is a mean life expectancy, not a typical adult lifespan. ADW's 'oldest recorded bird in the wild was 11 years' is a maximum and is not used. Wikipedia gives only '<5 years for wild birds'. No permissively licensed numeric value was found.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation, not a measured diet. Wikipedia: 'grasshoppers and other insects, lizards, mice, and small birds'. ADW's single urban study gave 78% insects and 14% mammals, with winter diet shifting to small prey. Invertebrate 0.65 and vertebrate 0.35 are judgement, covering a summer insect-heavy diet and a winter small-vertebrate diet.

traits.social.note: Judgement: pairs in the breeding season and solitary or loosely paired otherwise. Wikipedia describes seasonal sex differences in habitat use.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW (non-commercial, last resort): 'American kestrels are diurnal hunters'. Wikipedia describes perch-and-wait hunting but does not state the diurnal pattern.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flees to a new perch. The kestrel calls and mobs rarely; not sourced.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a midpoint value. Wikipedia describes urban and open-habitat use, which points away from high wariness.

habitat.note: Stratum shares and resource weights are judgement. Wikipedia: cavity nester, uses nesting boxes; ADW: open habitats and urban environments, tall perching sites for hunting.

seasonal.phases.note: ADW (non-commercial, last resort): 'In North America, the breeding season ranges from mid-April to mid-June.' Wikipedia gives incubation and fledging durations but no calendar months.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: 'Most birds breeding in Canada and the northern United States migrate south in the winter ... Birds that breed south of about 35° north latitude are usually year-round residents.' Partial migration applies across the range.

vocalizations.note: Wikipedia: the 'klee' is usually delivered as a rapid series when the kestrel is upset or excited. The cooldown is judgement.

look.note: Judgement: small falcon proportions (long pointed wings, short legs) and rufous-and-blue-grey palette, to be checked in the previewer.
